From router to receipt

One site first, then the rest.

A hotspot rollout lives or dies on whether the first router talks to the panel cleanly. That is where we start.

Connect the router

Add the site with its router address and API login. A test-connection button confirms the router answers.

Configure packages

Set price, duration, data limit and speed for each plan you want to sell, matched to a router profile.

Print and sell

Generate the first batch, print it as cards, and sell at the counter. Staff learn sell, activate and void in a day.

Add the next site

Each new router is another connection in the same panel, reporting into the same finance and inventory view.

Vouchers › Packages

Plans you define, limits the router enforces.

A package is the WiFi plan you sell. Set it once per site and every voucher you print carries its rules.

  • Price, duration, data limit and speed limit (for example 3M/1M)
  • Linked to the MikroTik hotspot profile that applies the limits
  • Active or inactive per package, scoped to each site
  • Packages lock once vouchers are issued, so pricing history stays honest
Hotspot › Vouchers › Packages
Vouchers › Generate Vouchers

A thousand vouchers in one click. Print them as cards.

Pick a package, enter a quantity, add an optional prefix. SentraGo creates a unique serial and PIN for each voucher and keeps every batch on record.

  • 1 to 1,000 vouchers per batch
  • Optional serial prefix up to 10 letters, so batches are easy to tell apart
  • Voucher Batches lists every batch with a Print cards button
Vouchers › Generate
Vouchers › Batches
Vouchers › Voucher Inventory

Find any voucher. Sell it, activate it, void it.

Sale and activation are separate steps. The router only ever sees a voucher that has actually been paid for.

  • Search by serial, filter by status or package
  • Serial, PIN, sold time and expiry on every row
  • Void removes an active voucher from the router straight away
  • Expired vouchers are removed automatically, every minute

Voucher lifecycle

Nobody is ever unsure whether a code is still live.

Every voucher moves through one strict path, and each step is logged against it.

Step 1

Unused

Generated in a batch with a unique serial and PIN. Not yet on the router.

Step 2

Sold

Sale recorded with amount, payment method and cashier.

Step 3

Active

Pushed to the router with the package's speed and data limits. Expiry is calculated.

Step 4

Expired or void

Removed from the router automatically on expiry, or straight away if voided.

Specification

The details your technician will ask about.

Router integrationDirect MikroTik RouterOS API. No RADIUS server required.
Voucher batches1 to 1,000 vouchers per batch, unique random serial and 6-digit PIN each, optional serial prefix.
Voucher lifecycleUnused, sold, active, expired or void. Each step is logged against the voucher.
PackagesPrice, duration, data limit and speed limit per package, scoped to a site. Locked once vouchers are issued.
Multi-siteUnlimited sites, each with its own router connection, packages and vouchers.
ExpiryA scheduled job expires vouchers and removes them from the router automatically, every minute.
Guest WiFiFree access with optional name, email and phone capture, code verification, session limits, wait time and speed limit. QR poster for each site.
Hotspot adsYouTube or MP4 video, full-page image, or login-page banner. Maximum play time 5 to 600 seconds.
SMSAny SMS provider with an HTTPS address, with a built-in test message.
FinanceSales and expense ledgers, recurring expenses, inventory valuation, sell-through, and P&L by package and category. CSV export.
Access controlAdmin and readonly roles. Finance and user management are admin only.
Client portalBranded captive-portal login served through the MikroTik walled garden.
Questions

Answers to what usually comes next.

Do we need a RADIUS server?

No. SentraGo talks to MikroTik directly over the RouterOS API. Hotspot users are created and removed on the router itself, which removes a whole layer of infrastructure most hotspot setups carry.

How do vouchers actually get sold?

A batch is generated with a serial and PIN per voucher, printed on a sheet of cards, and sold at the counter. The sale records the amount, payment method and cashier. Activation then pushes the voucher to the router with the right speed, data and time limits from its package.

Can we run more than one site?

Yes, from day one. Every site is its own router connection, and every package, voucher and report is scoped to a site, so head office sees each location without them interfering with each other.

What happens when a voucher expires?

A scheduled job checks every minute for vouchers past their expiry and removes them from the router automatically. Nobody has to remember to do it, and nobody stays connected for free because a task was missed.

Can we offer free WiFi as well as paid vouchers?

Yes. Guest WiFi is switched on per site. You choose the free time, how often a device can sign in, and whether to collect name, email or phone. You can also show a video or image ad before login.

Do we get proper financial reporting?

Revenue, expenses and net profit by day, month or custom period, inventory valuation on unsold vouchers, and a full P&L broken down by package and expense category. All of it exports to CSV.

Can staff without financial access still sell vouchers?

Yes. A readonly role can be used at the counter for day-to-day sales, while finance and user management stay restricted to admins.
